newsitem.title: UK: UK needs stronger regulation - futures expert.
newsitem.headline: UK needs stronger regulation - futures expert.

text.p: Britain's regulatory framework needs strengthening significantly in the light of the Sumitomo Corp copper scandal, an expert on futures markets said.

Professor Chris Gilbert of Queen Mary and Westfield College said in a paper to be presented at a London School of Economics seminar that manipulation on the London Metal Exchange (LME) would be more serious than on other futures markets.
It would distort the cash metal price which provided the pricing basis for the entire world copper industry.
"This underlines the importance of the LME and the regulator acting now to ensure that manipulation becomes much more difficult in the future," Gilbert said.

Gilbert said there was no basis for any charge that the LME lacked diligence in trying to identify and control manipulation, but he said that it and other London futures markets would benefit from a significant strengthening of the regulatory framework.
In June 1996, Japan's Sumitomo fired its former head trader Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he had run up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading.
